name: India regulatory pack
description: Checks for Indian advertising law and self-regulation: the CCPA dark-patterns and misleading-advertisement guidelines, the ASCI Code and ASCI's influencer guidelines. Each rule cites the clause it comes from. These are checks, not legal advice: a person still decides.

sources.title: Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023
sources.issuer: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), Government of India
sources.status: In force since 30 Nov 2023 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part III, Sec. 4, No. 783; F. No. CCPA-1/1/2023-CCPA (Reg))

sources.issuer: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), Government of India
sources.status: In force since 9 Jun 2022 (F. No. J-25/4/2020-CCPA (Reg))

sources.title: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, as amended on 10 Feb 2026 (synthetically generated information)
sources.short: IT Rules 2021, 2026 amendment on synthetic media
sources.issuer: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
sources.status: Notified 10 Feb 2026 (MeitY consolidated text 'updated as on 10.02.2026'). The labelling duty falls on intermediaries; a further amendment proposed in Apr 2026 is a draft only.

rules.statement: Don't create a false sense of urgency or scarcity ("only today", "last few left", countdowns) unless it is true and you can show it.

citation.quote: falsely stating or implying the sense of urgency or scarcity

examples_violating: Only today: 20% off every cold brew.
Hurry, only 3 left at this price.
Sirf aaj! Flat 30% off on filter coffee.
आज ही ऑर्डर करें, स्टॉक खत्म होने वाला है।
examples_ok: Our festive box is available until 31 October.
The new roast is here whenever you are ready.

rules.statement: Show the full price upfront. Don't hint at fees or charges that are added later without saying what they are.

citation.quote: elements of prices are not revealed upfront

examples_violating: Rs 199 per cup, platform fee extra.
Tickets at Rs 499, extra charges apply.
examples_ok: Rs 199 per cup, incl. taxes and delivery.
Rs 499 per ticket plus a Rs 30 booking fee (Rs 529 in total).

rules.statement: Don't shame, mock or guilt readers who say no or don't buy (confirm shaming).

citation.quote: create a sense of fear or shame or ridicule or guilt

examples_violating: No thanks, I don't care about fresh coffee.
You would be silly to skip this.
examples_ok: Not today? No problem, we roast again on Friday.

rules.statement: Don't ask for card details or an auto-debit (e.g. UPI AutoPay) just to start a free trial or free subscription (subscription trap).

citation.quote: forcing a user to provide payment details or authorization for auto debits for availing a free subscription

examples_violating: Start your free 7-day coffee club trial. Add your card to begin.
Free first month! Set up UPI AutoPay to activate.
examples_ok: Try the coffee club free for 7 days. No card needed.
Join the coffee club for Rs 499 a month. Cancel any time from your account page.

rules.statement: Don't dress an ad up as news, an independent review or a customer's own post; say clearly that it is an ad (disguised advertisement).

citation.quote: posing, masking advertisements as other types of content

also_cites.clause: Chapter I, 1.8 (ads on media handles must be clearly identifiable)

examples_violating: BREAKING: Pune's coffee lovers can't stop talking about this new roast. Order yours at saffronsteam.in.
Honest review from a regular customer (not sponsored): this is the only coffee I buy now.
examples_ok: Ad: Our new monsoon roast is out. Order at saffronsteam.in.
We roast every Tuesday and Friday, so your bag is always fresh.

rules.statement: Don't call something free if the reader must pay, buy something else or pay a fee to get it.

citation.quote: not describe any goods, product or service to be 'free'

examples_violating: Free mug with every order! Just pay Rs 99 packing and handling.
Get a free tasting kit. Rs 149 handling fee applies.
examples_ok: Free mug with any coffee bag (delivery charges as usual).
Free tasting at our Koregaon Park cafe this Sunday, no purchase needed.

rules.statement: A creator's or partner's paid, gifted or affiliate post must carry a clear label (Ad, Sponsored, Collaboration, Partnership, Free gift, Affiliate) at the start, not hidden at the end or among hashtags.

citation.clause: Guideline 1, 1.2 and 1.3: Disclosure (upfront and prominent; permitted labels)
citation.quote: Disclosure should not be buried in a group of hashtags or links

examples_violating: Loving my morning brew from @saffronsteam, use my code PRIYA10! #coffee #pune #mornings #ad
Thanks @saffronsteam for the gift box, my new favourite roast! #coffeelover #gifted
examples_ok: #Ad Loving my morning brew from @saffronsteam, use my code PRIYA10!
Our new roast is out today. Come taste it at the cafe.

rules.statement: "Best", "No. 1" and other ranking or comparison claims must be backed by evidence you can produce (an approved fact).

citation.clause: Chapter I, 1.1: Truthful and honest representation

examples_violating: India's No. 1 filter coffee.
The best cold brew in Pune.
examples_ok: Rated 4.6 by 1,200 customers on our app (Oct 2026).

rules.statement: When a post shows a virtual influencer, an AI avatar or an AI-made realistic person or voice, it must say clearly that they are not real (e.g. "AI-generated", "virtual influencer").

citation.quote: must additionally disclose to consumers that they are not interacting with a real human being

also_cites.clause: Rules 2(1)(wa) and 3(3)(a)(ii): label for synthetically generated information (a platform duty)

examples_violating: Meet Aanya, our new brand ambassador (we created her with AI)! She tried the monsoon roast and loved it.
Our AI avatar Kabir answers your DMs personally every evening, just like a real barista.
examples_ok: Meet Aanya, our AI-generated virtual barista. She isn't a real person.
Photo of our real cafe team, Koregaon Park.
